title: Trust in the Lord: Proverbs 3:1-10
speaker: Unknown Speaker
summary: This lesson explores Proverbs 3:1-10, emphasizing the importance of trusting God with all your heart rather than relying on your own understanding. The speaker explains that the Proverbs are addressed to the covenant community of believers and contain truisms about how life generally works when we obey God's commands. The passage demonstrates temporal blessings that come from obedience, mercy, truth, and complete trust in the Lord's direction.

outline.title: Understanding Proverbs as Covenant Teaching
subpoints: Proverbs are written to the covenant community, not general advice for everyone
Proverbs are truisms—generally true statements about how life works, not absolute promises
The Father instructs his son in God's ways and desires obedience with the whole heart

outline.title: Temporal Blessings from Obedience
subpoints: Obeying God's law brings long and peaceful life
Mercy and truth bring grace in God's sight and man's sight
Trusting in the Lord makes paths straight
Fearing the Lord and departing from evil brings health to flesh and strength to bones
Honoring the Lord with possessions brings financial prosperity

outline.title: The Character of Mercy and Truth
subpoints: Mercy and truth must characterize the believer's life
Binding them around your neck means keeping them close to your heart
God and humanity both appreciate lives marked by mercy and truth
These virtues should be grown in and lead to God's blessings

outline.title: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart
subpoints: Trust is complete confidence without doubt or analysis
Implicit trust means obeying without questioning, like sitting on a chair
Trust is based on evidence and God's character
We naturally tend to trust ourselves rather than God
Trust must be constantly reminded and practiced through prayer, Bible study, and meditation

outline.title: Leaning Not on Your Own Understanding
subpoints: Leaning on understanding means making it your life's support
Our own thoughts cannot be trusted as ultimate guidance
God's thoughts and ways are higher than ours
We must think with a heavenly mind through Christ
Trusting our understanding ultimately leads to falling and failure

outline.title: Acknowledging God in All Your Ways
subpoints: Every step and area of life should acknowledge God's lordship
Acknowledging God comes through knowing Jesus as Savior
Prayer helps us acknowledge God constantly
Bible study and meditation on Scripture enable us to know God's will
God promises to make our paths straight when we acknowledge Him in all things

outline.title: Living the Gospel in Light of These Commands
subpoints: Trust in Christ because He perfectly trusted the Father where we have failed
Jesus never leaned on His own understanding but always obeyed His Father
Christ's perfect obedience is credited to all believers
Our salvation rests on Christ's perfection, not the perfection of our faith
The gospel frees us from self-reliance by exposing the bankruptcy of self-confidence
God makes our paths straight, not necessarily easy, but with His presence
Live one day at a time, trusting God for today rather than worrying about tomorrow

transcript:
## Opening Scripture Reading

> "My son, do not forget my law, but let your heart keep my commands; for length of days and long life and peace they will add to you. Let not mercy and truth forsake you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart, and so find favor and high esteem in the sight of God and men. Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding. In all your ways, acknowledge him and he shall direct your paths. Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the Lord and depart from evil. It will be health to your flesh and strength to your bones. Honor the Lord with your possessions and with the first fruits of all your increase. So your barns will be filled with plenty and your vats will overflow with new wine." (Proverbs 3:1-10)

## Understanding Proverbs as Covenant Teaching

Sometimes we read the book of Proverbs and think it was written for everybody, but that is not the case. Remember that Solomon is speaking to the covenant community—he is speaking to his sons in the church, in the family, as it were, the church of his time. The book of Proverbs requires faith in Christ. It is written for those who have professed faith in the Messiah. It is written for the covenant community of God, and that is what we have here. So it is not just general thoughts for anyone, but for those who trust in the Lord Jesus Christ, for those that follow him.

The book of Proverbs is also a book of truisms. What that means is that these are things that are generally true. It does not mean that they will happen 100% of the time, but that is how usually life works. It is equivalent to saying, statistically speaking, this is the way things go, which means generally that is the way things go. We have a category for that in our thinking and in our language, and that is what we read in the book of Proverbs. Usually that is how life works. Are there exceptions? Yes. So they are not necessarily promises or commands, but they are how things generally work there.

What we have here is the Father who continues to instruct the Son in the ways of the Lord. If you look at verse one, that is how the passage begins: "My son, do not forget my law, but let your heart keep my commandments." In the book of Proverbs, the words of the Father are the words of God. These are the things that the Son should hear, and the Father wants the Son to follow God with his whole heart.

## Temporal Blessings of Obedience

One of the things we see here that the Father wants to communicate with the Son is that there are temporal blessings in obeying God. Now that is a concept that we are scared of. I think we have been so scared of the prosperity gospel that we have tried to detach any temporal blessings from obedience to the Lord, lest we be called a disciple of Joel Osteen or something like that. But this is something that the Bible teaches. There are temporal blessings in obeying God and his word.

In verses one and two, the Father says, "Do not forget the law so that you are going to have long and peaceful life." In verses three and four, "Do not forsake mercy and truth so that you are going to have grace in the sight of God and man." In verses five and six, "Trust in the Lord and your path will be straight." In verses seven and eight, "Do not be wise in your eyes, and that is going to generate health." In verses nine and ten, "Honor the Lord with your possessions and you will prosper in your finances."

You can see here that there is a connection between obeying God and the temporal blessings of the Lord. But one of the things we see in the book of Proverbs is that the Father uses every opportunity to get across the need to follow God's law. This Father is intent to get his children to follow the Lord, to follow his law. So in verse one, it says, "My son, do not forget my law. My commands, which are the commands of God." It is generally true that people who obey God live blessed lives, even healthier lives. That is what we find here in this passage.

## Mercy and Truth Must Characterize Us

We also see in verses three and four that mercy and truth must characterize us. The Father says, "Let not mercy and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart and so find favor and high esteem in the sight of God and man."

Now this is a particular way of saying that we must not forsake mercy and truth, but let not mercy and truth forsake you. Stay close to them. Abiding in God's mercy and in God's truth. Be characterized by mercy and truth. It says, "Bind them around your neck." Now it is important that you understand that the Father here is not prescribing some new type of neckwear, like a tie or necklace. When he says, "Bind them around your neck," when you bind something around your neck, where does it sit? On your heart, right? That is the idea. Have the law of God written on your heart. Keep it close to your heart.

The Father says that God approves of a lifestyle marked by mercy and truth, and so does humanity. That is not just something that God appreciates, but people around us also appreciate that. That is something that we are to grow in, and we are going to see the blessings of the Lord in that.

## Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

He also commands us to trust in verse five: "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding." To trust is to have complete confidence. When Malachi trusted that the chair would hold him, he had implicit trust. Without any question, he trusted that my command for him to sit was to be obeyed, and he also trusted that the chair would hold him up.

Trust is this complete confidence. None of you checked the pew before you sat to make sure that the pew would hold you up. There is this implicit trust. And that is what the Lord calls us to do—to have implicit trust, not to doubt him every time he tells us to do something, not to have to analyze every time that he tells us to do something, to have this implicit trust.

And yet there is a trust that is based on evidence. We have all kinds of reasons to trust in the Lord. This command is here because it is something we have to be always reminded of. The last time you worried, what were you doing at that time? Not trusting. The less time you spent worrying, you were trusting. You can see that this is something we need to be reminded of again and again and again. We find that a lot in the book of Proverbs and the book of Psalms. These remind us to trust in the Lord. We have a tendency to forget to trust in the Lord. We end up trusting in other things, especially in ourselves. If we are going to err, we are going to err by trusting in ourselves. So there is a need to look to God at all times.

Remember the passage in Hebrews 12, which talks about the cloud of witnesses. The cloud of witnesses are encouraging us, are clapping for us as we are in our race. And one of the things they are encouraging us to do is to run our race, shedding everything that is going to keep us from getting to the end—sin and other things that so easily ensnare us. But they are encouraging us to run in a certain way. Remember what that way is? Look into Jesus, right? Look into Jesus who is the author and finisher of our faith. That is the same thing as running trusting. Trusting in Jesus, you are going to get to the end. He is going to be there. You run trusting that way.

So the Father says, "Trust in the Lord." And then he gives us the how: "with all your heart," without any reservation, just completely dedicated to the Lord. Jesus says the same thing with different words. Remember when he was asked, "What is the greatest commandment in the Bible?" His answer was to love the Lord with everything that makes you, and then to love others as yourself. To love the Lord with everything that makes you is to trust in the Lord.

God is so gracious to us. He does not leave us alone to figure out what we should believe about him or what he wants us to do, what we should have in our heart. But he gives us all that in his word. The Heidelberg Catechism asks, "What do the scriptures principally teach?" That is, where is the Bible mainly about, primarily about? "The scriptures principally teach what we are to believe concerning God and what duties he requires of us." In trusting, he does not leave us to ourselves. He tells us, he shows himself, he tells us what he expects. Have you ever worked for a boss or even your parents where they expect you to do something, but they never tell you what the expectations are or how you are going to do that? It is a very frustrating thing. But that is not how our Father in heaven is. He is clear about what he expects of us and what he wants us to do.

## Lean Not on Your Own Understanding

In the second half of verse five, it says, "and lean not on your own understanding." Do not lean. To lean means to use as a crutch, to make something your life depends on it.

When the two Josiahs leaned on each other, as they took steps forward, the more they leaned into it, both ended up falling. And that is not what the Lord is saying to you. That is not what the Lord wants us to do. He wants us to lean not on our understanding. Leaning on our understanding would be like leaning on each other and eventually falling. Do not lean on your own understanding—what you think is right—without the illumination of the Spirit of God through the word of God. He wants us to lean not on our understanding, but lean on him and his understanding.

Remember that passage in Isaiah 55 where the Lord says, "My thoughts are higher than your thoughts and your ways higher than your ways." People think that means we cannot think God's thoughts. That is not what the passage means. What the passage means is, "Come to my level." That is what God is saying. Come and think the way I think. Do not think your thoughts. Do not lean on your own understanding. Lean on my understanding.

Colossians 3 says that you who have been raised with Christ think with a heavenly mind. We are to lean on him, to lean on his understanding.

## Acknowledge Him in All Your Ways

The proverb says that we are to, in all our ways, acknowledge him in verse six. Every step we take is under his direction. The idea is to know him in all your ways. Every area of life—thought life, belief life, action life, words, life, attitude—everything you acknowledge God. You are drinking a cup of water, you are acknowledging God. You are eating, you are acknowledging God. You are having a conversation with somebody, you are acknowledging God. God is master over that.

How do we do that? Well, we cannot do that without knowing Jesus as our Savior first. That is the only way that we can acknowledge God—to know him through Jesus Christ. But we also cannot constantly acknowledge God if we are not praying to him. So prayer is another way that helps us acknowledge God. Studying the Bible, we cannot really acknowledge God if we do not know what God is saying. So that is meditation on the Bible, thinking about what the Bible says.

It is great to read the Bible through the year, and you have to do it a few times in your life. But I do not think that is what you should do every year, because there is a tendency to make getting through the Bible your goal and forget to actually meditate upon what you are reading. So do it a few times in your life. You do not have to do that every year. It is more important that you actually get and think about what you are reading and then incorporate it into your life.

And there is a promise there in verse six: "In all your ways, acknowledge him and he shall direct your path." The idea of "direct your path" is to make it straight—in the sense of making it easier to obey and making it so that it is clear where you are going. That is what the idea is here, to level it. Much like in Isaiah 40, which talks about the ministry of Elijah, who was going to raise the valleys and lower the mountains for the path of the Lord. That is the idea here.

There is a great difference, brothers and sisters, between the path of the one who trusts in God and the one who does not. Proverbs 13:15 says, "Good understanding gains favor, but the way of the unfaithful is hard." The way is written as bumpy, not straight like Proverbs 3, but bumpy, hard, difficult.

In Psalm 23, talking about the way of the righteous, the Psalmist says, "He restores my soul. He leads me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake."

## How Shall We Live? Trust in Christ

So how shall we live in light of this passage? First thing: trust in Christ because he perfectly trusted the Father where we have failed. Proverbs 3 commands us to trust in the Lord with all our heart, but let us be honest—do we do that? If you are in doubt, the answer is no. Every one of us has leaned on our own understanding. Every one of us has refused to trust in the Lord. We trust our wisdom, we trust our plans, we trust our feelings, we trust our strength more than we trust the Lord.

The gospel begins to expose those failures. The gospel begins to expose how we on our own cannot do what this proverb tells us to do. The good news is that Jesus Christ is the only wise Son. He did these things perfectly—100% of the time—and continues to do them. He never leaned on his own understanding but always submitted himself to his Father's will, even when the path led to Gethsemane and the cross. His perfect obedience is credited to all who believe in him.

Therefore, our acceptance with God rests not on the perfection of our trust, but on the perfection of Christ's trust and obedience. That is why we do not need perfect faith. What saves us is not the quality or the quantity of our faith. What saves us is the one in whom we believe. And any kind of faith in that one saves. Did you get that? Even faith that is as small as a mustard seed is sufficient to save you.

## Let the Gospel Free You from Self-Reliance

Secondly, let the gospel free you from self-reliance. The greatest obstacle to trusting God is not ignorance, but self-confidence. Most of the time we do not trust in God not because we do not know who he is, but because we just trust in ourselves more. We naturally believe that we know best, can solve our own problems, and can secure our own future.

One of our seminary professors used to say that students come to seminary to learn a little Greek and Hebrew and to teach theology. We tend to be very self-confident in everything concerning us. But the cross also exposed the bankruptcy of self-reliance. If we could save ourselves through our own wisdom, Christ would not have needed to die.

So the gospel calls us to renounce our confidence in ourselves and to rest entirely in Christ.

## Follow Christ Confidently

Thirdly, follow Christ confidently because he is directing your path. The promise that God will make our path straight does not mean life will always be easy or free of suffering. Jesus himself perfectly acknowledged the Father in all his ways, yet his path led through rejection, suffering, and the cross before it led to resurrection glory. That is why he can promise that through the valley of the shadow of death—which is not necessarily talking about death, but the darkness of life—he is going to be with us. Not take us out of it, but be there with us.

Brothers and sisters, because we are united to Christ, God is directing our paths in the same loving way. Even when we cannot understand his providence, we know its destination. Whatever is happening is to conform us to Christ, is to conform us to eternal glory, so we can obey him today, even without seeing every step ahead, confident that our shepherd never leads his people aimlessly.

Brothers and sisters, what Jesus wants you to do today is just live today. Trust him today. Do you know what he wants you to do tomorrow? Trust him tomorrow. Live that day. And then for Tuesday, the same thing. To worry about tomorrow today is to carry tomorrow with today's strength. God never gives us strength to carry two days at a time. So it is just a waste of effort. God calls us to obey him today. The one who gave his life for us will faithfully complete the work he has begun in us and will safely bring us home. But he does it hour by hour, minute by minute, not month by month, week by week. So we do not trust our own understanding. We trust in him. We do not lean on our understanding, but we trust in the Lord with all our heart, so that he might direct our paths.
